newsitem.title: INDIA: India Birla, AT&T tie up phone finance deal.
newsitem.headline: India Birla, AT&T tie up phone finance deal.

text.p: Birla-AT&T Communications Ltd, a joint venture between India's Aditya Birla group and U.S.-based AT&T, said on Wednesday it had completed the financing of its $1.5 billion project to set up a mobile telephone network in three western Indian states.
It said the financing was completed following a $283 million loan syndication arranged by Bank of America NT&SA through its subsidiary BA Asia and Toronto Dominion (Southeast Asia) Ltd.

The loan syndication, which comprises a foreign currency portion and a rupee tranche, involves India's biggest non-recourse external commercial borrowing in the telecommunications sector, the company said in a statement.

The Birla group holds a 51 percent stake and AT&T 49 percent in the venture, which has been licensed by the Indian government to provide cellular telephone services in the states of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Goa.
"The financing will allow Birla-AT&T to continue one of the fastest cellular network roll-outs in India," the statement said.
